title: Volitional form (意向形) — “let's ～ / I will ～”
summary: The volitional form is the plain form of ～ましょう. It is used to invite someone (“let's ～”) or to state your own intention (“I think I'll ～”) in casual speech.

patterns.form: Ⅰ類（五段）：語尾 u段 → o段 ＋ う
patterns.gloss: 行く → 行こう / 休む → 休もう / 登る → 登ろう

patterns.form: Ⅱ類（一段）：る → よう　／　Ⅲ類：する → しよう、来る → 来（こ）よう
patterns.gloss: 食べる → 食べよう / 見る → 見よう / する → しよう / 来る → 来よう

body.p: For godan verbs, change the last sound to the o-row and add う (書く → 書こう). For ichidan verbs, replace る with よう (食べる → 食べよう). する becomes しよう and 来る becomes 来よう (こよう).
Use it to invite friends (週末は海へ行こう) or to decide for yourself (少し休もう). The polite version is 行きましょう. With ～(よ)うと思う you can also state an intention that is not yet fixed.
It is casual, so it sounds unnatural to someone of higher status. When used for your own decision, it shows little interest in the listener's opinion, so it can sound close to an order.

examples.ja: 週末（しゅうまつ）は海（うみ）へ行（い）こう。
examples.tr: Let's go to the sea this weekend.
examples.note: 行く → 行こう (godan: k + u → k + ō).

examples.ja: 疲（つか）れたから、少（すこ）し休（やす）もう。
examples.tr: I'm tired, so let's rest a little.

examples.ja: 今度（こんど）の休（やす）みに、山（やま）へ登（のぼ）ろう。
examples.romaji: Kondo no yasumi ni, yama e noborō.
examples.tr: Let's climb a mountain on the next holiday.

pitfalls: Do not treat ichidan verbs like godan verbs: it is 食べよう, not 食べろう.
To a superior, use ～ましょう; ～よう is for friends and family.
